data.title: Suspicious debt collection demand from EuroClaim (€287.40)
data.summary: EuroClaim Forderungsmanagement Ltd. (Cyprus) demands €287.40 for an alleged phone-concluded lottery subscription, payable by 6 August 2026 to a Lithuanian account held by a private person. It shows several scam indicators.
data.explanation: This letter claims you owe €287.40 for a lottery subscription (Gewinnspiel-Abonnement) supposedly concluded by phone. It has many hallmarks of a scam or at least a dubious claim: a 72-hour ultimatum, threats of account seizure and criminal charges, payment to a foreign account in a private person's name, and added fees. Do not pay under pressure. If you know of no such contract, you can dispute the claim in writing and ask for proof of the contract. Consider contacting a consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale) or a lawyer, and report it to the police if it looks like fraud. Note that a real collection agency cannot seize your account without a court order.

items.consequence: The letter threatens account seizure, a negative SCHUFA entry and a criminal complaint; these threats are unverified.

warnings: Payment is demanded within 72 hours to a Lithuanian IBAN held by a private individual, a strong scam indicator.
The letter threatens account seizure, a SCHUFA entry and criminal charges without a court order, which is not how lawful collection works.
The letter says objecting is pointless, which is false; you may dispute an unfounded claim.
The salutation is generic and the fees (€84 collection, €24 processing) look inflated.
The letter gives no details of the alleged contract, its date or the creditor's address.
